# Host C long bounds expand from LONG_MAX; reversed bounds preserve existing branch precedence.
outlier_score([-1], {LONG_MAX}, {LONG_MAX}) => error:integer overflow
outlier_score([{LONG_MAX}], 0 - {LONG_MAX} - 1, -1) => error:integer overflow
outlier_score([0, 0], {LONG_MAX}, {LONG_MAX}) => error:integer overflow
outlier_score([{LONG_MAX}, {LONG_MAX}], 0, 0) => error:integer overflow
outlier_score([0, 1], {LONG_MAX}, {LONG_MAX}) => error:integer overflow
outlier_score([0], {LONG_MAX}, {LONG_MAX}) => {LONG_MAX}
outlier_score([-1], {LONG_MAX} - 1, {LONG_MAX} - 1) => {LONG_MAX}
outlier_score([{LONG_MAX}], 0, 0) => {LONG_MAX}
outlier_score([{LONG_MAX}], 0, 1) => {LONG_MAX_MINUS_ONE}
outlier_score([], 1, 3) => 0
outlier_score([1, 3, 8, 5], 3, 6) => 4
outlier_score([0], {LONG_MAX}, 0) => {LONG_MAX}
outlier_score([0], 1, -1) => 1
outlier_score([1], 1, -1) => 2
fn score(xs) { outlier_score(xs, 3, 6) }; score(reverse([8, 3, 1])) => 4
0 && outlier_score([-1], {LONG_MAX}, {LONG_MAX}) => 0
if 0 { outlier_score([{LONG_MAX}], -1, -1) } else { 7 } => 7
outlier_score(1, 0, 1) => error:expected array
outlier_score([1], [0], 1) => error:expected integer
outlier_score([1], 0, [1]) => error:expected integer
outlier_score([1], 0) => error:wrong argument count
let n = 0; let total = 0; while n < 65 { total = total + outlier_score(reverse([1, 3]), 2, 2); n = n + 1; }; total => 130
